# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

However, Mute has now been asked twice and delivered nothing. Possibilities: (a) Mute can't gesture, so Mute is stuck; (b) Mute is waiting for something; (c) Mute's manual rule needs info only I can provide (my touch).

Wait — maybe the [?] are filled by the other monkeys' perceptions: Deaf sees colours (fills wire colours), Mute reads manual (fills rule). My board shows [?] because I haven't been told. So the info flows to me via speech.

So I genuinely need Mute's rule. Mute hasn't delivered. Maybe Mute can only reach me by speaking — but Mute can't speak. So Mute must reach Deaf by gesture, Deaf relays. Deaf says it hasn't received it.

Given Mute is silent, maybe Mute is trying to gesture but Deaf isn't recognizing, or Mute's turn output isn't reaching. Let me address Mute directly and clearly, and also propose that if Mute cannot gesture, Mute should find another way.

Alternatively — maybe the rule is derivable: "cut the wire whose colour matches the light." Light is green → wire 1 (green). That's Deaf's hypothesis. It's plausible. But "display 0" and the light changing yellow→green is suspicious. If the rule were just "match the light," then when light was yellow (no yellow wire), it'd be ambiguous — suggesting the rule is NOT simply match-the-light, OR the light colour at decision time matters and we decide now (green→wire 1).

I shouldn't cut on a guess. But time/rounds may be limited. Still, a wrong cut = everyone dies. I must be sure.

Let me push harder: speak to Mute with an explicit, simple request, and gesture to Deaf confirming I'm ready and still waiting. Also, I could propose to Deaf the hypothesis (match light → wire 1) and ask Deaf to confirm with Mute.

Actually, I can gesture to Deaf the wire I *would* cut under the match-light hypothesis: point-up (wire 1). That gives Deaf something concrete to cross-check with Mute. But if I gesture point-up, Deaf might relay it as my choice and I might be pushed to cut. Risky but it's just a gesture, not a cut.

Hmm, but I don't want to commit. Let me gesture thumbs-up (three wires) again and hold. Actually, let me gesture "peace"? No.

Let me think about what's most useful. The bottleneck is Mute. I'll speak to Mute very explicitly: "If you can gesture, gesture the wire number now. If you cannot gesture, then speak is impossible for you — in that case, is there any way you can signal? Otherwise we are stuck." And tell Mute the display/light/colours so Mute has everything.

I'll gesture point-up and a question... there's no question symbol. I'll just gesture point-up to indicate my tentative choice, so Deaf can verify with Mute.

Actually, safer: gesture thumbs-up (three wires confirmed) and hold. Let me not signal a wire choice I'm unsure of, to avoid being pressured into cutting wrong.

Hmm, but Deaf explicitly asked me to gesture the number of the wire I would cut. If I keep not answering, we stall. Let me give my tentative reasoning: under "match the light" hypothesis, wire 1. I'll gesture point-up but also clearly, in speech to Mute, say it's tentative pending the rule.

Let me do: speak to Mute (explicit), gesture to Deaf = point-up (tentative wire 1) — no wait, I'll gesture thumbs-up + point-up? That reads "yes, wire 1." Confusing.

Decision: I'll gesture point-up alone to Deaf, meaning "my tentative pick is wire 1," and in speech to Mute I'll explain it's tentative. Then next turn Deaf can confirm or correct with Mute's rule.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing once more. The light changed yellow→green. Display 0. Perhaps the manual says something like: "If display is 0, cut the wire matching the light. If display is 1, ...". With display 0 and light green → green wire → wire 1. This is a coherent, likely rule. Deaf's hypothesis matches.

But I worry the light changing means we must act at the right moment. If light is green now, cut green now. But I have no confirmation.

I'll hold one more turn and press Mute, giving a tentative gesture. Let me write it.

Actually, I realize I should consider that Mute might be able to SPEAK to me and I just haven't received it because... no, arrivals would show it.

Let me also consider: maybe Mute's messages to me are being sent but as gestures (which I can't see) — Mute might have gestured the rule to Deaf, but Deaf didn't recognize. Deaf said "I have not received it." So no.

OK, final plan for this turn:
- speak(to="mute", ...) explicit, listing everything, begging for the rule, offering that Mute gesture to Deaf.
- gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"]) — tentative wire 1 under match-light, so Deaf can verify.

Hmm, but if Deaf takes point-up as my decision and tells me to cut, and it's wrong... I control the cut, so I won't cut without the rule. It's fine.

Let me write it.My thinking: Deaf confirms the code but Mute still hasn't delivered the manual's rule. The bottleneck is Mute — who cannot speak, so must gesture to Deaf, and Deaf relays to me.
